questions.scenario: Mummy is coughing badly. What do you do?

options.text: I physically go to the kitchen, crush ginger, boil water, and make a strong 'kadha'.
I check the cough syrup bottle to see if it has 'Dextromethorphan' for dry cough.
I add honey and lemon to the kadha so it tastes and smells much better for her.
I quickly run to the 24/7 chemist shop and buy the best syrup they recommend.

questions.scenario: When you buy a new shampoo or face wash, what do you notice first?

options.text: I just apply it to see if it lathers well and cleans effectively.
I read the back label to check if it has harmful chemicals like Parabens or Sulfates.
I notice the beautiful packaging, the color of the liquid, and the fragrance.
I check the price tag to see if it was worth the money.

questions.scenario: In the Chemistry Lab at school, what is your favorite part?

options.text: Physically pouring chemicals into test tubes and mixing them.
Calculating the exact atomic mass and balancing the equations in my notebook.
Watching the chemical reactions change into beautiful pink or blue colors.
I usually just organize the group, tell others what to do, and write the final conclusion.

questions.scenario: You have to organize the messy 'Medicine Box' at your home.

options.text: I sit down and physically sort all the loose tablets and strip packets into boxes.
I check the expiry dates and Google what the unknown tablets are actually used for.
I label the boxes beautifully with colorful markers like 'Headache', 'Fever', etc.
I throw away the old ones and make a budget list to order a fresh medical kit from 1mg.

questions.scenario: What kind of YouTube videos related to science do you watch?

options.text: Cool home experiments where people mix Diet Coke and Mentos.
Deep animated videos explaining how viruses mutate and vaccines work.
Videos on how skincare serums or organic perfumes are made in factories.
Case studies on how companies like Sun Pharma became multi-million dollar giants.

questions.scenario: If you had to launch your own product, what would it be?

options.text: A fast-acting energy drink or protein powder that I mixed myself.
A groundbreaking pill that cures a complex disease like Dengue instantly.
A high-end, glowing skincare face cream that smells amazing.
A massive chain of 24/7 smart medical stores across India.

questions.scenario: You visit a local pharmacy to buy medicines for your grandparents.

options.text: I watch how fast the chemist physically finds the exact medicine from 1000s of boxes.
I ask the chemist if this medicine has any side-effects with their other pills.
I look at the vitamin gummies and wish normal medicines also tasted that good.
I ask for a 10% discount or look for generic alternatives to save money.

questions.scenario: You are making a fruit smoothie. What is your process?

options.text: I throw everything in the blender, chop fast, and make it instantly.
I calculate the exact protein and calorie count of the fruits I am using.
I garnish it beautifully with mint leaves and serve it in an aesthetic glass.
I make a big batch and jokingly tell my siblings it will cost them ₹50 a glass.

questions.scenario: Which 'boring' task can you tolerate the best?

options.text: Standing all day in a lab coat, mixing chemicals carefully.
Looking into a microscope for hours or reading 100 pages of chemical formulas.
Testing the smell of 50 different raw oils until I find the perfect one.
Calling 50 doctors a day to convince them to buy my company's medicine.

questions.scenario: What title fits you the best in your friend group?

options.text: The Fixer (Always ready with a quick practical solution).
The Nerd (Knows all the random scientific facts).
The Aesthetic One (Always has the best skincare, perfumes, and style).
The Hustler (Always knows how to negotiate and get things done).

Clinical_Pharmacist.title: Clinical Pharmacist
Clinical_Pharmacist.primary_match_text: You are practical, organized, and love hands-on work! You enjoy understanding how things mix together to create immediate physical results.
Clinical_Pharmacist.day_in_the_life: Working in top hospitals, ensuring doctors prescribe the right chemical combinations, and dispensing life-saving medicines.
Clinical_Pharmacist.alternative_match_text: Because you love practical mixing and health, you would also excel as a Clinical Dietician or a Laboratory Technician.
Clinical_Pharmacist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB or PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Pharm (Bachelor of Pharmacy) or Pharm.D.

Drug_Research_Scientist.title: Drug Research Scientist
Drug_Research_Scientist.primary_match_text: You are the scientific mastermind! You have a highly analytical brain that loves diving deep into formulas, molecules, and finding cures.
Drug_Research_Scientist.day_in_the_life: Working in high-tech labs, studying diseases under a microscope, and discovering new vaccines or cancer pills.
Drug_Research_Scientist.alternative_match_text: Your love for deep scientific analysis makes you a perfect fit for Biotechnology, Genetics, or Microbiology.
Drug_Research_Scientist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Chemistry/Biotech or B.Pharm, followed by an M.Sc/Ph.D. in Pharmacology.

Cosmetic_Scientist.title: Formulation / Cosmetic Scientist
Cosmetic_Scientist.primary_match_text: You perfectly blend chemistry with aesthetics! You care about how health products look, smell, feel, and benefit the skin.
Cosmetic_Scientist.day_in_the_life: Working in labs for brands like L'Oreal or Mamaearth, formulating new glowing serums, lipsticks, or organic shampoos.
Cosmetic_Scientist.alternative_match_text: If you want a highly creative scientific field, your aesthetic sense makes you perfect for Perfumery or specialized Dermatology.
Cosmetic_Scientist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB/PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Chemistry or B.Pharm, followed by a diploma/master's in Cosmetic Science.

Pharma_Business_Manager.title: Pharma Business Manager / Medical Entrepreneur
Pharma_Business_Manager.primary_match_text: You have a pure business brain. You understand science, but you are much more interested in sales, marketing, and building a medical empire.
Pharma_Business_Manager.day_in_the_life: Meeting top doctors, launching new medicines in the market, or running a massive chain of pharmacies.
Pharma_Business_Manager.alternative_match_text: With your commanding nature and negotiation skills, you would easily excel as a Hospital Administrator or a Tech Startup CEO.
Pharma_Business_Manager.roadmap: Take Commerce or Science in 11th/12th. You can do a B.Pharm or BBA, followed by an MBA in Pharmaceutical Management.
